In article <313E09...@studio.disney.com>, Robert Goudie
<robert...@studio.disney.com> wrote:

> I mentioned these two points in the VTES-L list on the subject of vote
> pushing:

Hello again. :)

> People oppossed to vote pushing often assume that after a vote is
> completed the vote pusher will refill his hand back up to seven fresh
new
> vote cards.

Actually, no. That is not my assumption, but the problem is that even if
the vote fails (due to others pushing votes), the vote push deck will
almost certainly be able to pass the next, because there percentage is
higher (given that no one else is playing vote push).

A vote push(VP) deck has ~75% vote cards. A typical vote(V) deck will
have ~35% vote cards. A typical non-voting(NV) deck will have ~1% vote
cards.

Pretend the first vote fails. Everyone pushes. The VP deck will regain
5 votes. The V deck will have likely pushed twice and regained 1 vote.
The NV deck will have pushed all votes, and likely regained none. At
this point, The VP will only need to push once to win the vote. With the
Praxis Seizures the VP deck will have, it will soon only push votes to
get the damaging votes in hand.

>Most vote decks will have 20-25% master cards which cannot
> be quickly cycled through. After each vote there is often a residual
> master (or other non-vote) card that sneaks into your hand.

This is quite true. But, it is also insignificant. By the time the
Master cards start "clogging" the hand, it is usually after a few votes.
Theoretical Example:
Master after
Turn Master Votes
1 1 6 (Call none)
2 0 7 (Call 1, push 6), 5 (Call 1, push 4), 4 (Discard)
3 1 (w/ D) 6 (Call 1, push 5), 4 (Call 1, push 3), 3
4 2 (w/ D) 5 ...

Note the _slow_ increase. Also realize that after the first or second
turn, the number of vote pushes will decrease as everyone else runs out
and your seizures get passed. Eventually Master clog ends, even with
weenie vote push (where 7 or more votes can be passed in turn 4)

>I have a
> low-mid. capacity Nosf. political deck (I got tired of all my politics
> being intercepted.) that works well. I came in 2nd. place at a
> convention in Los Angeles a couble of weeks ago. 2 times my hand got 5
> master cards in it. Even after a "Deal with the Devil" (I had to put
> the "Deals" in because the hand jam really has been a problem.) I
> replaced my eight (Elder Library) cards with a hand full of Praxis
> Siezures. My next vote was, of course, quite successful but then I
> replaced those and began collecting residual master cards again.

> The other common drawback to this deck is the running out of Library
> cards. If no one else has any titles or votes you're OK. But decks
with
> IC members and other high-capacity vampires were quite common at the
> convention (and in my regular group).

That means your deck is not working like a typical WVP. If you are
playing low-mid Nossies (2 to 6, I imagine), you are runnning about 3 to
4 times _slower_ than a WVP. The WVP will eat alive anyone trying to get
out a Inner Circle member. That's 11 pool (down to 19) and 3 to 4 turns.
Turn 1) 3 Vamps average
Turn 2) 1 to 2 Seizures, total of 3 votes. (1.5 damaging votes ~7 pool)
Turn 3) 0 to 1 Seizures, total of 4 votes (3.5 damaging votes ~10 pool)
Turn 4) 0 to 1 Seizures, total of 5 votes (4.5 damaging votes ~21 pool)
At this point, there will be roughly 2.5 Princes (5 votes). If the IC
member is out in turn three, 1 vote or bleed will kill.

Let's send one vampire to torpor a turn.

That's ~6 less damaging votes by turn 4. Still doing 20 pool to your prey.

>I run out of library at least
> half of the time I play this deck. I ran out at the tournament and
ended
> up in second place. The guy who won (a guy from my playgroup and my
> original Grandprey) did 3 Second Traditions + Eagles sight to wreck a
few
> key votes. Anyone in my playgoup is free to vote push and it has never
> been a problem for us. Just my $0.02.

Everyone may be free to vote push, but only the vote decks get the benefit.

I played in another playgroup and they played 4CL/No GT. I happened to
have a deck that was nearly 4 CL (6 Majesties), and they let me play it.

I decimated them.

Why?

ALL my votes passed. They pushed occasionally, but since they were not
playing vote decks, they weren't able to keep up. If I pushed away
useless votes (at the time), I had a high probability of getting a useful
one. If they pushed a vote, they almost never would redraw one. By the
time they got a prince or two out (four player game), I had already
gotten two and used a seizure. At this point, pushing became an
excercise in card cycling and augmenting Voter Captivation.

Vote pushing doesn't lead to a balanced game. The only time a WVP deck
will be hindered is if someone else is playing vote push politics or
someone gets Justine with a Sports Bike. Rush comes out to slowly, who
cares if they are intercepted, and its quicker than S&B. Regular
politics can't compete. In a role-playing sense, how does it work? Do
the Caitiff just shout really loudly to get their way despite the fact
that princes may oppose them? The Methuselah may manipulate Camarilla
politics, but if all it is doing is manipulating puny, untitled Caitiff,
how much influence can it have?

Vote pushing, in short, leads to a broken, nonsensical game.

Messages.Author: CurtAdams
Messages.Body:
Robert Goudie <robert...@studio.disney.com> writes:

>I mentioned these two points in the VTES-L list on the subject of vote
>pushing:

>People oppossed to vote pushing often assume that after a vote is

>completed the vote pusher will refill his hand back up to seven fresh new

>vote cards. Most vote decks will have 20-25% master cards which cannot
>be quickly cycled through.

That's too many masters for most decks. It means you should only be
playing 4-5 non-masters per turn, including actions, modifiers, and
reactions. Even for a non-pushing vote deck that's too few, e.g. Vote
card #1 (intercepted) + 2 Fortitude cards + Vote card #2 + Bewitching
Oration + Deflection as a reaction (6 cards total) is a pretty minimal
turn for a Ventrue vote deck. That would indicate 15% Masters as a goal.

In any case, with vote pushing you can freely put even fewer masters into
your deck - if you don't have a master, keep pushing till you draw one.

>I came in 2nd. place at a
>convention in Los Angeles a couble of weeks ago. 2 times my hand got 5
>master cards in it. Even after a "Deal with the Devil" (I had to put
>the "Deals" in because the hand jam really has been a problem.) I
>replaced my eight (Elder Library) cards with a hand full of Praxis
>Siezures. My next vote was, of course, quite successful but then I
>replaced those and began collecting residual master cards again.

You definitely have too many masters. Throw out 1/2 your masters, at
random, and you deck will improve.

>The other common drawback to this deck is the running out of Library
>cards. If no one else has any titles or votes you're OK. But decks with

>IC members and other high-capacity vampires were quite common at the

>convention (and in my regular group). I run out of library at least

>half of the time I play this deck. I ran out at the tournament and ended

>up in second place. The guy who won (a guy from my playgroup and my
>original Grandprey) did 3 Second Traditions + Eagles sight to wreck a few

>key votes.

If you have enough Praxis Seizures (and not too many masters) you
shouldn't have a problem . However, if vote decks are common, weenie
voters don't do too well as they have too much opposition (both titles and
counter-pushing).

Curt Adams (curt...@aol.com)

>At this point, there will be roughly 2.5 Princes (5 votes). If the IC

I went 1st last night... and with my whole one transfer put out
Smudge. Next turn, I bleed to get the edge (which I held about 3
turns) and because I had no "good" aggressive votes. Next turn 2
Praxis, and a Reversal of Fortune (just for the heck of it, a mistake
I see now.. made the game amusing though). Then prince # one gets
havened and into torpor. I had to fight the torpor battle all game.
Not fun at all. Anyway... like I said it was a _very_ bad game for
the deck.

>Let's send one vampire to torpor a turn.

Depends on other things, but if you don't have to push much, you can
probably get away with losing one of you princes to torpor.





>I decimated them.




Despite the fact that I did not get a victory point last night,
re-enforced in my mind was the fact that WVP is abusive and it does
not make sense in a role playing way. If the Ventrue/Gangrel vote

And boring... and unenjoyable.

but feel its something that has to be done, sorta like the
equiptment/stealth deck I'm going to have to put together to "use "

>> Praxis, and a Reversal of Fortune (just for the heck of it, a mistake
>> I see now.. made the game amusing though).

>Just curious, why did you think it was a mistake?

Correction on my part... I had an agressive vote...KRC, but wanted to
play a cons. ag, which I didn't have. Or I could have played another
Praxis, which I would have done if I had know 3 haven uncovereds were
coming my way. I went into brain lock, saw that I had the one
Reversal of Fortunes that I put in the deck in my hand and said...
looks like fun. It wasn't a terrible move, but the KRC would have
been much better (though it did slow a prince down from getting into
the game, which was a _good_ thing).

>> Then prince # one gets
>> havened and into torpor. I had to fight the torpor battle all game.
>> Not fun at all. Anyway... like I said it was a _very_ bad game for
>> the deck.

>...and you were still "that" close to running the table with it. If your
>pred and grandpred hadn't elected to put out a prince with our first
>vampire, you might have been unstoppable.

Which is unfotunate. WVP should not work... but it does, to damn
well. At the very least, it totally messes up the prey/pred
relationships on the table.
Actually, what I think doomed me was when my gradprey got out a prince
(and probably the ventrue HQ). Without the HQ my prey _never_ would
have passed any votes, in particular the conserv. ag. that did 5 to me
(a game changing happening). Without that prince (which brought on
table votes to 4 for me, 9 for everyone else) I would have been able
to pass occasional votes. Heck I think I got one passed after that by
convincing you to either abstain or vote for me.
All and all, there were about 4 diferent things I could point to that
shut me down: the vote deck pred (and his HQ), the 3 haven uncovereds
(in consecutive turns), my mistake not to get a 3rd prince, the fact
that _everyone's_ princes came up. Remove any one or 2 or them, and
I would have been getting some victrory points move likely.

>> >Vote pushing, in short, leads to a broken, nonsensical game.
>> And boring... and unenjoyable.

>Yep. Can't wait until our group decides that unlimited vote pushing is a
>"Bad Thing". Maybe we need an out of turn master that affects voters the
>way that Archon Investigation (?) affects big bleeders. <chuckle>

Bureaucratic Overload may start to show up, which is a minor bother.
Or everyone can pack a surprise influence. :)

>that happens (in other words, the 2nd time I played the weenie stealth

Bingo. If I wanted to "win" whatever you want to call the stats thing
we're keeping, I would play WVP almost exclusively. I'd have to trade
for a couple of Parity Shift (since I've only got 4/5), think up a
better way to gain blood, remove a handful of the Domain Challeges,

easily) to the point where it won ~90% of the time with no other VP
decks at the table, and ~50% other wise.
Also have to learn when to cut my losses, aka cut deals with any other
VP decks at the table so as to at least salvage a victory point.

And unless I get really bored, I'm not going to play WVP for a while.
Its a crappy strategy, and if someone shows up with one I'll just lose
and say we should adopt at least the vote fix Golden Tenant. And play
my own WVP the next week.

This is laughable to the WVP deck. As quickly as you are sending them to
torpor, new ones are coming out. A good WVP deck uses Infohighway and
Effective Management for Masters.

Turn "Weenie" Vamp Average
1 3 (Haven Uncovered placed at this time is removed)
2 4 (Haven Uncovered placed at this time on becomes effective)
3 5
4 6
etc...

You need to be sending _more_ than one vampire to torpor a turn. Not
only that, they have to be the important ones.

If you use small vamps, they will have to spend time hunting after
combats. If you use larger vamps, you will be near death by the time you
get one out. The major problem is, you have to be able to send out
_alot_ of minions at the weenie horde, and the weenies just keep coming.
As a predator, your back is open. As a prey, your prey works the WVP
Decks great-grand prey for it.

Things change once you get to "the Game of Three". With only 3 players
left, the others will typically work together. But this is tenuous at
best. All unblocked votes will pass (with _rare_ exceptions). Only if
both decks are combat ready can a chance for survival exist, and even at
dropping 2 vamps per turn (starting with turn 3, things look rough.

It will take (in a 3 player game) 8 damaging votes fully hitting one
player to oust them (average, including a 10 point allocation for vamps
influenced). The next player would require about 2.5 damagin votes to be
ousted (average, including a 15 point allocation for vamps influenced).
Turn
1 3 Vamps
2 1.5 princes, 1.5 damaging votes, 4 vamps
3 2 princes, 3.5 damaging votes, 5 vamps - 2 torped (.8 princes torped)
4 2.5 princes, 2.5 damaging votes, 6 Vamps - 4 torped (1.65 princes
torped)
5 3.0 princes, 1.5 damaging votes, prey ousted, 7 Vamps - 5 torped

at this point it is over. The WVP is bringing out a vampire a turn and
losing one a turn, and still calling enough votes to oust its new prey.

I can't figure it out. How would you plan to "beat the crap out of this

deck" with a typical deck? Inquiring minds want to know.

Most people don't do anything of the sort. If you're not playing a
serious combat deck, rush cards like that are pretty useless. Even many
intercept combat decks will be shy on rushes. Further, rush combat is
necessarily only a moderately important part of the Jyhad deck mix. If
many people play rush, then rush cards aren't very useful, so you're
better off pursuing other strategies.

>Now with both predator and prey
>going for it, Strike:combat ends/untaps will be used up to
>end combat and (through the concerted effort) at least one
>little bod will enter torpor even if you're only doing 1 hand
>damage with everyone. Most decks though have a limited
>combat capacity and thus it will be slightly easier.

A "solution" to weenie vote push which relies on both predator and prey of
the deck playing the same (somewhat uncommon) style AND that they
cooperate to to trash the "problem" deck (which requires their other
enemies nor be much of a threat) - isn't much of a solution.
